data.description:
# Magnet Creates Pull Animation

## Problem statement

When the Magnet power-up (P9) is active, nearby power-up drops are pulled toward the ship at `MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED`, but the visual representation (the `graphics` object) does not update its position — only the logical `x`/`y` coordinates change. The player cannot see the magnet pulling power-ups in, making the effect feel invisible and unintuitive.

## Users

- **Players** — want to visually see the magnet effect: drops should visibly slide toward the ship along a direct path, changing direction when the ship moves.
- **Developers** — need the animation to be consistent with the existing simulation step (`tick(dt)`) and the current magnet attraction math.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to see power-up drops visibly slide toward my ship when the Magnet is active, so I can understand the range and strength of the effect.
- As a **player**, I want the pull direction to update in real time when I move, so the animation feels responsive and natural.
- As a **developer**, I want the visual position to stay in sync with the logical drop position used by the collection logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Visual sync:** Every frame, each drop's `graphics` object position is set to the drop's current `x`/`y` coordinates so the player sees the drop move.
- **AC2 — Direct path pull:** Drops within magnet range move along the shortest path toward the ship (already handled by the existing `_applyMagnet` logic computing `dx`/`dy` and stepping toward the player).
- **AC3 — Direction updates:** If the player moves while a drop is being pulled, the drop changes direction to follow the ship (the `dx`/`dy` calculation each frame naturally handles this).
- **AC4 — Existing tests pass:** The existing magnet test (`'applies the P9 magnet effect, and the magnet pulls a drop toward the ship'`) continues to pass, asserting `drop.x` moves toward the ship.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- The change must be minimal — touch only the visual position sync, do not alter magnet math, radius, or attraction speed.
- The animation must stay deterministic (same `tick(dt)` semantics — no frame-rate-dependent animation easing).
- No new Phaser dependencies or particle systems.

## Existing state

- `_applyMagnet(dt)` in `GymPowerUps.ts` correctly updates `drop.x` and `drop.y` each frame when magnet stacks > 0.
- `advanceDrops(dt)` updates `drop.graphics.setScale(drop.powerUp.currentScale)` but does NOT update the graphics position.
- `graphics.setPosition(x, y)` is called only once at spawn time — never during magnet attraction.
- The result: drops move logically (test assertions on `drop.x` pass) but appear stationary (the graphics stays at spawn position).

## Desired change

Update the graphics position each frame to reflect the current logical drop position. The correct approach is to add `drop.graphics.setPosition(drop.x, drop.y)` inside the magnet attraction loop in `_applyMagnet`, after each drop's `x`/`y` is updated — this ensures the visual position follows the logical position in the same iteration. An alternative is a dedicated `_syncDropPositions()` call after `_applyMagnet` in `tick()`, but the loop-local approach is more efficient (only updates drops within magnet range).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — Add `drop.graphics.setPosition(drop.x, drop.y)` in the `advanceDrops` method (or in the magnet attraction loop).

## Related work

- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** — Add a Magnet power up (GDD spec; completed).
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ** — Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math (completed; tests assert `drop.x` moves toward ship).
- **AH-0MTCO0M3C002Y67S** — GymPowerUps scene wiring (completed; implements `_applyMagnet`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** Keep to position sync only — do not add particle trails, glow effects, or easing animations. These are nice-to-have but belong in separate items.
- **Assumption:** The existing `drop.x`/`drop.y` logic in `_applyMagnet` is correct (it is tested and audited). Only the visual sync is missing.
- **Assumption:** Updating position in `advanceDrops` is the right place — it runs after magnet attraction and before collection, keeping the visual pipeline tidy.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the pull animation be smooth/eased or snap to the logical position each frame?" — Answer (derived from context): Snap to logical position each `tick(dt)` step, matching the existing deterministic simulation model. No easing or interpolation needed. Source: the codebase uses deterministic `tick(dt)` steps throughout.
- Q2: "Should any visual effect accompany the pull (particle trail, glow intensification)?" — Answer: Not for this work item. The operator's brief is about making the effect visible, not decorative. Decorative extras are scope-creep.
data.title: Magnet creates pull animation

data.description:
Epic (from RCA of AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG) — the playable game (PlayScene) has diverged from the gym scenes: several power-up behaviours that the gyms exercise (and that the GDD requires) are not wired into PlayScene.

## Root cause

PlayScene was authored as a parallel scene (AH-0MU72SZP1005X14G onward) that re-implemented game logic instead of extending the shared patterns the gym scenes exercise. The power-up features (magnet pull, teleport, shield/phase visuals, per-type audio) were implemented and tested **only against gym scenes**; their work-item ACs referenced gym scenes, never PlayScene. The shared modules (effects.ts, Player.ts) hold the registry/math, but the scene-level wiring of those effects exists only in gyms. As a result collecting P5/P9/P7 in the game does nothing visible, and P3/P6/P4 lack the gym's visual feedback.

Gym scenes are meant to exercise production code; the game must exercise the same code. Each child item below fixes one deviation.

## Deviations found (gym → game)

1. **P9 Magnet pull missing in PlayScene** — GymPowerUps._applyMagnet pulls drops + visual sync (AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG); PlayScene._updateDrops has no attraction. Even the shared combat base lacks it.
2. **P5 Speed Boost not applied in PlayScene** — GymPowerUps calls player.setSpeedMultiplier(effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()) every tick; PlayScene never calls it.
3. **P7 Teleport missing in PlayScene** — GymPowerUpsCombat + GymFormationScene have S/↓ → findTeleportDestination → consumeTeleport → P6-on-arrival; PlayScene has no teleport handling at all.
4. **P3 shield bubble visual missing** — GymPowerUpsCombat draws a shield bubble; PlayScene absorbs hits (tryAbsorbShield) but shows no bubble and gives no blink after absorb.
5. **P6 phase ghost visual missing** — GymPowerUpsCombat makes the ship semi-transparent while phased; PlayScene only skips collisions, no ghost alpha.
6. **P4 bomb notice missing** — GymPowerUpsCombat flashes 'BOMB! Bullets cleared'; PlayScene clears bullets but no notice.
7. **Player weapon fire audio missing** — GymWeapons._playShootCue plays per-weapon cues; PlayScene._autoFire plays none.
8. **Per-type pickup activation audio missing** — GymPowerUps/GymWeapons play unique cues per type (GDD §7.3); PlayScene plays only the generic chime.
9. **Enemy-specific destruction audio missing** — GymFormationScene prefers entity.playDestructionAudio() (e.g. Diver/Tank/Boss unique sounds); PlayScene always plays the generic sound.

Child items fix each deviation, preferring shared/module-level implementations so gyms and game exercise the same production code.
data.title: Restore gym-game parity: wire missing power-up behaviours into PlayScene (RCA)

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 1 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). The magnet power-up (P9) does nothing in the playable game: drops are never pulled toward the ship.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when I collect a Magnet (P9) during a run, all on-screen power-up drops should visibly slide toward my ship so the effect is observable (matching the GymPowerUps gym, AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG).

## Existing state
- GymPowerUps.ts implements the _applyMagnet logic: each collectible drop within the magnet radius (2x ship size + 50% per stack) moves toward the ship at MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED, with the drop graphics position synced to the logical position each frame (visual sync, commit 81624e8).
- PlayScene _updateDrops (src/scenes/PlayScene.ts) advances lifecycles and collection only — no magnet attraction at all.
- EffectsRegistry.magnetStacks() accumulates correctly in PlayScene (collect via applyCollect('P9')); nothing consumes it.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — In PlayScene, when magnetStacks() > 0, each collectible drop within the magnet radius is moved toward the player each tick step at MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED (reuse the radius helper from powerups/effects.ts and constants).
- **AC2** — The drop graphics position is updated to its new logical x/y each frame (visual pull animation, as in AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG).
- **AC3** — Prefer a shared, module-level magnet-attraction helper used by BOTH GymPowerUps/combat gyms and PlayScene, so gyms and game exercise the same production code (per RCA root cause). Refactoring GymPowerUps to call it is acceptable; behaviour must not regress.
- **AC4** — Unit tests: magnet pull moves a drop toward the ship; drop beyond radius is not pulled; overlapping drop is collected; stacked radius grows with stacks.
- **AC5** — All existing tests (incl. gym magnet tests) continue to pass; full suite green.

## Constraints
- Do not change magnet math, radius, attraction speed, or GDD §4.4 semantics (permanent, cap 5 stacks).
- The shared combat gym base (GymFormationScene) also lacks magnet pull — if the shared helper is added, wire it there too so gyms remain parity references.
data.title: PlayScene: wire P9 Magnet pull attraction (visual pull animation)

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 2 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). Collecting P5 Speed Boost during a run does nothing: the ship speed never changes.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost (P5) I expect +50% thrust/max-speed for 10 s (GDD §4.4), exactly as demonstrated in the GymPowerUps gym.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUps.ts tick() calls player.setSpeedMultiplier(effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()) every frame, so P5 boosts movement live.
- PlayScene tick() drives input/physics (player.physicsTick) but NEVER applies the speed multiplier — setSpeedMultiplier is not called anywhere in PlayScene.
- EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier() returns 1.5 while P5 is active; the Player supports live multiplier application.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene applies the registry speed multiplier to the player ship each tick (setSpeedMultiplier(effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier())), so P5 visibly boosts movement for its 10 s duration.
- **AC2** — The multiplier is re-applied every frame (P5 is timed — must return to 1 after expiry) and survives respawns during an active P5.
- **AC3** — Prefer applying the same integration the gym uses; if a shared helper exists/extracted, gym and game both use it.
- **AC4** — Unit tests: P5 active → speedMultiplier applied (movement config scaled); P5 expired → multiplier back to 1; re-collect refreshes duration.
- **AC5** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change P5 duration, multiplier, or registry semantics.
- Note: the shared combat gym base (GymFormationScene) also never applies the speed multiplier — if addressed via shared code, wire it there too so gyms remain parity references.
data.title: PlayScene: apply P5 Speed Boost multiplier live

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 3 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). The P7 Teleport power-up does nothing in the playable game: there is no S/↓ handling, no safe-spot resolution, and collected teleport stacks can never be consumed.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when I collect a Teleport (P7) and press S or ↓, I expect to warp to the nearest safe spot in the direction of travel (free of enemies and bullets, clamped to screen bounds), consuming one stored stack, and gain P6 Phase Shift on arrival (GDD §4.4) — exactly as in the combat gyms.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUpsCombat.ts and GymFormationScene.ts both implement _handleTeleport (S/↓ JustDown), triggerTeleport, findTeleportDestination (safe-spot resolver in powerups/teleport.ts), effectsRegistry.consumeTeleport() (FIFO stack + P6 via applyPhaseShift), movement-state sync, and a position update.
- PlayScene has NO teleport handling: no S/↓ key binding beyond WASD movement, no triggerTeleport, no safe-spot call. _collectDrop calls applyCollect('P7') so stacks accumulate in the registry but can never be used.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene binds S and ↓ as teleport-activation keys (JustDown semantics, so movement still works — S is also move-down in the 4-directional scheme, matching the gyms).
- **AC2** — Pressing S/↓ with at least one stored P7 stack warps the player to the nearest safe spot in the direction of travel via findTeleportDestination (enemy + bullet avoidance, screen-clamped), consuming one stack FIFO and granting P6 Phase Shift.
- **AC3** — Pressing S/↓ with zero stacks does nothing; no auto-repeat teleports.
- **AC4** — Player movement state (velocity/position used by physicsTick) is kept in sync after the warp, mirroring the gym implementation.
- **AC5** — Unit tests cover: teleport with stacks (warps, consumes, P6 granted), no stacks (no-op), destination respects enemy/bullet safety, and S/↓ input handling.
- **AC6** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Reuse the shared findTeleportDestination + registry consumeTeleport — do not duplicate resolution logic in PlayScene.
- Teleport activation is S or ↓ per GDD §2.1/§2.3 (already changed from Space in AH-0MTV7KAGZ006ER8R).
data.title: PlayScene: wire P7 Teleport (S/↓) with safe-spot resolution

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 4 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). P3 Shield absorbs hits in PlayScene, but there is no shield bubble visual and no post-absorb invulnerability blink.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when my shield (P3) is active I want to SEE the shield bubble around my ship, and when a hit is absorbed I expect the bubble to pop and a brief invulnerability blink, matching the GymPowerUpsCombat gym.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUpsCombat.ts _updateVisuals draws a shield bubble (lineStyle + low-alpha fill circle radius SHIP_SIZE*1.6) around the ship while effectsRegistry.isShielded, and _handleHits pops the shield (tryAbsorbShield) then _startInvulnerability() for a short blink.
- PlayScene _hitPlayer() calls effectsRegistry.tryAbsorbShield() — the hit is correctly absorbed (no life lost, AC of the combat gym) — but no bubble is rendered and no blink runs after absorb.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene renders a visible shield bubble around the ship while P3 is active (mirror the GymPowerUpsCombat visuals; depth above gameplay).
- **AC2** — When the shield absorbs a hit, the bubble disappears and the player gets the brief invulnerability blink (same as gym hit-response), so the absorb is observable.
- **AC3** — Prefer a shared visual helper if one is extracted, so gym and game render the bubble identically (scope: extraction optional; duplication acceptable if kept minimal per RCA constraints).
- **AC4** — Unit tests: bubble visible while shielded; after absorb bubble gone + invulnerable window started + life NOT lost.
- **AC5** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change shield duration (15 s), absorb semantics, or GDD §4.4 behaviour.
data.title: PlayScene: add P3 shield bubble visual + post-absorb blink

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 5 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). P6 Phase Shift grants pass-through in PlayScene, but the ship does not become visually ghosted.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when P6 Phase Shift is active I want to SEE my ship become semi-transparent/ghostly, signalling intangibility, matching the GymPowerUpsCombat gym.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUpsCombat.ts _updateVisuals sets the ship alpha to 0.45 while effectsRegistry.isPhased (ghost), restoring alpha 1 when it expires (and not clobbering the invulnerable blink while that is active).
- PlayScene tick() skips collision checks when isPhased (pass-through works — PlayScene.ts line ~821), but never changes the ship's alpha, so the player cannot tell the effect is active.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene renders the ship as a semi-transparent ghost (alpha ~0.45) while P6 is active; full alpha restored on expiry.
- **AC2** — The ghost alpha does not clash with the post-hit invulnerability blink (mirror the GymPowerUpsCombat precedence: if invulnerable, keep the blink alpha; else ghost alpha).
- **AC3** — Unit tests: alpha 0.45 while phased; alpha 1 after expiry; blink-vs-ghost precedence.
- **AC4** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change P6 duration (3 s) or pass-through behaviour.
data.title: PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual

Gym=>game deviation 6 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). P4 Bomb clears enemy bullets in PlayScene, but the player gets no visual confirmation and no distinct audio.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when I collect Bomb (P4) I expect a clear 'BOMB!' flash + the on-screen enemy bullets to clear, matching the GymPowerUpsCombat gym.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUpsCombat.ts _collectDrop on P4 calls _clearEnemyBullets() and _flashBombNotice() (centered 'BOMB! Bullets cleared' label for ~1.2 s).
- PlayScene _collectDrop handles P4 (clears enemy bullets via _clearEnemyBullets — line ~1049) but shows no notice.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene shows a short centred 'BOMB! Bullets cleared' notice (or equivalent) on P4 collection, mirroring the gym (a label or HUD flash of similar prominence).
- **AC2** — P4 continues to clear all on-screen enemy bullets and does not damage enemies (unchanged, GDD §4.4).
- **AC3** — Unit tests: bomb notice visible after P4 collect; auto-hides after its timeout; bullets cleared.
- **AC4** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change P4 semantics (no enemy damage).
data.title: PlayScene: add P4 bomb-clear visual notice

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 7 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). The player's weapons are silent in the playable game: no per-weapon fire cues.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, I want to hear the distinct fire sound of each weapon I have equipped (cannon, spread, dual, rapid), matching the GymWeapons gym and GDD §7.3 player audio palette.

## Existing state
- GymWeapons.ts _playShootCue(weaponId) plays playCannonFireSound/playSpreadFireSound/playDualFireSound/playRapidFireSound once per firing weapon per volley (audio funcs exist in src/audio/effects.ts).
- PlayScene _autoFire (src/scenes/PlayScene.ts ~line 642) fires weapons via player.tryFire but plays NO sound at all.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene plays the per-weapon fire cue for each weapon that fired in a volley (one cue per weapon, not per bullet), mirroring _playShootCue.
- **AC2** — The cues are safe no-ops without an AudioContext (they already are, per audio module design).
- **AC3** — Unit tests: firing the cannon plays the cannon cue; cycling through spread/dual/rapid plays the corresponding cue; no cue when nothing fired. (May assert via the audio module's test seam.)
- **AC4** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change weapon timings, rates, or bullet behaviour.
- If a shared 'fire cue dispatch' helper is extracted from GymWeapons, use it in both gym and game.
data.title: PlayScene: add per-weapon player fire audio cues

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 8 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). Power-up collection in PlayScene always plays the generic pickup chime — no per-type activation cues.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, I want a unique, recognisable activation cue for each power-up I collect (additional to the generic chime or replacing it), so I know at a glance which bonus I got — per GDD §7.3 'Pickup activation cues are unique per pickup type and distinct from the generic collection chime'.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUps.ts plays per-type cues on collect: playSpeedBoostCollectSound (P5), playExtraLifeCollectSound (P8), playMagnetCollectSound (P9).
- GymWeapons.ts plays per-type weapon pickup cues: playSpreadPickupSound/playDualPickupSound/playRapidPickupSound/playResetPickupSound.
- PlayScene _collectDrop always plays only playPowerUpCollectSound() regardless of type — P5/P8/P9/weapon drop activation cues (which exist in src/audio/effects.ts) are never played in the game.
- Note: GymPowerUpsCombat and GymFormationScene also use only the generic chime — the per-type cues exist only for the subset shown in those gyms. The game should match the GDD spec and the gyms that DO implement per-type cues.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene plays the appropriate per-type activation cue on collect for each distinct type: P3 shield, P4 bomb, P5 speed, P6 phase, P7 teleport, P8 extra life, P9 magnet, and weapon drops (spread/dual/rapid/reset) — matching the GDD §7.3 palette and reusing the existing audio functions. Where no dedicated cue exists in the audio module for a type, use the generic chime (documented gap, create a separate audio work item if a new cue is needed).
- **AC2** — Behaviour of collection (effects applied) is unchanged.
- **AC3** — Unit tests: collecting each type triggers its cue via the audio test seam; generic fallback for types without dedicated cues.
- **AC4** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change effect semantics or drop logic.
- Keep cues safe no-ops without AudioContext.
data.title: PlayScene: add per-type power-up pickup activation audio

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 9 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). Enemy destruction in PlayScene always plays the generic destruction sound; per-enemy destruction audio is ignored.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, I want enemies to sound distinct when destroyed (e.g. the Diver's unique destruction sound, Boss's destruction sound), matching the combat gyms and the per-enemy audio character in docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

## Existing state
- GymFormationScene (shared combat gym base) prefers entity.playDestructionAudio() when the entity exposes the seam (Diver → playDiverDestructionSound, Boss → playBossDestructionSound via playDestructionAudio) and falls back to the generic playDestructionSound otherwise. It also avoids double-playing on player-body collision.
- PlayScene._handleCollisions always calls destroySelf() + playDestructionSound() for enemies (lines ~783, ~844), never calling playDestructionAudio — so Diver/Boss (and any future per-enemy audio) sound generic in the game.
- Entities already implement the playDestructionAudio seam (Diver.ts:291, Boss.ts:863); Tank has playTankDestructionSound in the audio module.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene plays each enemy's specific destruction audio where the entity exposes playDestructionAudio() (e.g. Diver, Boss), falling back to the generic sound otherwise — matching the gym base behaviour.
- **AC2** — No double-play: on player-body-vs-enemy collision (step 4), the enemy destruction audio is played once (gym base plays entity audio there and lets _hitPlayer own the generic player-hit sound).
- **AC3** — Unit tests: bullet kill of a Diver plays the diver sound (via audio seam); a generic enemy plays the generic sound; collision path plays exactly once.
- **AC4** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change enemy damage, scores, or kill logic.
- Prefer sharing the destruction-audio dispatch with the gym base if a helper can be extracted without behaviour change.
data.title: PlayScene: use per-enemy destruction audio (playDestructionAudio seam)
